title: How ZIA API changes become live: saving versus activating

prose.text: A ZIA write is not live until it is activated {{saved-not-live}}, and the activation call is separate from the write, although ending a session can activate on its own [[zia.terraform.activation-methods:session-end-autoactivation]]. The Terraform side of this is in [[zia.terraform.activation]], and the product-level lifecycle across ZIA and Cloud and Branch Connector is in [[shared.activation]].

prose.label: The calls.
prose.text: {{sdk-activation-endpoints}} {{oneapi-sample-activate}} Which path the legacy guide names is in dispute {{divergence:activate-path-differs}}. The Python call names are in [[zia.sdk-python.client-errors-and-accessors:activation-accessor]].
Whether a pending End User Subscription Agreement blocks activation is open {{gap:eusa-precondition}}.

checks.do: Whether the activation status reads PENDING or INPROGRESS after a write, before looking for a platform fault.
Which activate path the client calls: the SDK and the OneAPI sample use POST /status/activate; the legacy PDF names POST /status.

saved-not-live.statement: The vendor's URL Categories API guide says to activate configuration changes after making them, by sending a POST request, so changes made through the API are saved but not live until then.

quotes: After making any configuration changes, ensure that you activate them by sending a POST request to /status.

sdk-activation-endpoints.statement: The Python SDK's activation client reads the activation status with a GET to /status and activates configuration changes with a POST to /status/activate.

quotes: Returns the activation status for a configuration change.

oneapi-sample-activate.statement: The OneAPI contract documents POST /status/activate as the call that activates saved configuration changes, and the OneAPI Getting Started guide says ZIA configuration changes must be explicitly activated with it.

expect.description: Activates the saved configuration changes. To learn more, see Saving and Activating Changes in the ZIA Admin Portal.

quotes: Activation might be required: For ZIA and Cloud & Branch Connector APIs, configuration changes must be explicitly activated with a POST to /status/activate or /ecAdminActivateStatus/activate, respectively.

oneapi-sample-activate.conditions: Re-sourced on recapture (2026-10-18): the OneAPI sample-endpoints page it cited no longer exists; previously "The OneAPI sample endpoints document POST /zia/api/v1/status/activate as the call that activates saved changes, required after any ZIA configuration change."

status-values.statement: The activation call returns a status of ACTIVE, PENDING or INPROGRESS.
status-values.conditions: Re-sourced on recapture (2026-10-18) from the removed sample-endpoints page to the OneAPI contract's response schema.

activate-path-differs.summary: The legacy URL Categories guide says to activate by POSTing to /status, while the SDK and the OneAPI contract use POST /status/activate.

positions.says: Activation is a POST request to /status.

quotes: by sending a POST request to /status.

positions.says: Activation is a POST to /status/activate; GET /status only reads the status.
The OneAPI contract activates with POST /status/activate.

expect.description: Activates the saved configuration changes. To learn more, see Saving and Activating Changes in the ZIA Admin Portal.

activate-path-differs.impact: A client that follows the PDF literally and POSTs to /status would not call the endpoint the SDK uses; use the activate path.

eusa-precondition.title: Whether EUSA acceptance gates activation
eusa-precondition.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the EUSA status endpoints "enforce a click-through user agreement that must be accepted before certain config changes are activatable" and are "a precondition for activation in some tenants". The Activation API tag carries GET /eusaStatus/latest and PUT /eusaStatus/{eusaStatusId}, and acceptedStatus false means an 'agreement pending' state, but no source ties EUSA acceptance to activation succeeding.
eusa-precondition.blocks: diagnosing an activation that fails on a tenant with a pending EUSA

activation-duration.title: How long a ZIA activation takes, and how often to poll it
activation-duration.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Activation typically completes in 1-3 minutes. Do not poll faster than every 30s.' No captured source gives a typical completion time or a polling interval.

queue-and-invalid-states.title: What activation returns while changes are queued or invalid
queue-and-invalid-states.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Status STATE_PROCESSING_QUEUE_DEPTH_NOT_ZERO (409) means other changes are queued; STATE_INVALID (409) means a pending change has a config error that blocks activation until it is fixed or reverted.' The captured status values are ACTIVE, PENDING and INPROGRESS (status-values); neither 409 code appears in a captured source.

any-admin-activates.title: Whether any admin can activate another admin's pending ZIA changes
any-admin-activates.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Anyone with admin access can activate your pending changes, including a different automation script or a human admin.' Related: zia.terraform.activation:activation-scope asks whether an activation publishes only the caller's changes or every admin's; no captured source settles either question.

no-drop-pending.title: Whether pending ZIA changes can be discarded without activating them
no-drop-pending.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'There is no API to drop pending changes without activating them; the only undo is to re-write the original values.' The OneAPI guide says a change cannot be reverted once activated (shared.oneapi.write-practices:activation-zia-cbc), and no captured source says whether a staged change can be discarded.
